title: Citus: failover test (kill a worker Patroni leader -> standby promoted, VIP follows, queries continue)
description: The future nexus-cli CitusAdapter `failover-test` verb -- stops nexus-patroni on the current worker1 leader, watches Patroni promote the streaming standby, confirms the keepalived VIP (.212) floats to the new leader (so pg_dist_node needs no rewrite), and proves a cross-shard aggregate still returns through the coordinator. Destructive (forces a real failover) but self-healing -- restarts the stopped node to rejoin as replica.

observe.what: old worker1 leader stopped -> Patroni elects the standby -> VIP .212 rebinds on the new leader -> SELECT count(*) FROM events still returns 800+ -> stopped node restarted + rejoins as replica
sudo /usr/local/sbin/nexus-patronictl list citus-worker1 -- Leader flips between the two nodes
ip -4 addr show dev nic0 -- VIP .212 appears on whichever node is the leader
sudo -u postgres psql -h /var/run/nexus-citus -d citus -c 'SELECT count(*) FROM events' -- routed through coordinator, unaffected by the worker failover

whatProves: A worker Patroni failover is invisible to the coordinator: registering workers by VIP means the keepalived-floated VIP moves to the promoted standby and pg_dist_node stays valid -- distributed queries continue with no metadata rewrite. PG-native sharding + Patroni HA compose.
